title: Lanthanoid analysis in seawater by seaFAST-SP3™ system in off-line mode and magnetic sector high-resolution inductively coupled plasma source mass spectrometer
author: Soto-Jiménez, Martinez-Salcido, et al.
materials: Sample's introduction into the Thermo Scientific™ Element XR™ High-Resolution ICP-MS is performed in off-line mode with an ESI SC autosampler integrated system (4 DX Autosampler with Dual Flowing Rinse). The eluted sample is introduced into the instrument through a micro-Flow PFA nebulizer (200 µL min−1) into the Peltier PC3 (Elemental Scientific Inc., USA) cooled quartz impact bead spray chamber (Fig. 1). This chamber acts as a collision-reaction cell to remove interferences that degrade the detection limits. Then, the sample is introduced into an argon plasma as aerosol droplets (nebulized).

The high-resolution inductively coupled plasma source mass spectrometer (HR-ICP-MS) is one of the best techniques to determine lanthanoids (La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Tb, Er, Tm, Yb, and Lu) in seawater [6]. In particular, the Thermo Scientific™ Element XR™ is a Nier-Johnson inverse geometry (e.g., focused on energy and mass/charge) dual-focus sector magnetic ICP-MS instrument that is widely used in multi-elemental determinations (e.g., lanthanoids) in complex sample matrices (e.g., seawater). A schematization and description of the lanthanoids analyses procedure by HR-ICP-MS is provided in Fig. 2. All measurements were performed in off-line mode with Thermo Scientific™ Element XR™ with an ESI SC autosampler integrated system. The measurement was conducted as ‘Triple’ detector mode, automatic switching using the Element software. Detailed instrumental conditions and the operating parameters for optimizing and ion lens voltages to achieve high and reproducible signals are provided in Tables 2 and 3. External calibration solutions of lanthanoids were prepared daily by increasing additions of a multi-element stock standard solution (10 mg L−1 lanthanoids in 2% HNO3, High-Purity™ Standard). External standardization was applied using a six-point calibration (1, 5, 10, 50, 100, and 1000 ng L−1, Fig. 3). Calibration solutions were processed through the SeaFAST-SP3™, such as the samples. Blank solutions of 2% HNO3 and NaCl matrix in 2% HNO3 were used as an instrumental blank, measured before each sample and standard. An internal 115In standard solution of 100 µg L−1 was prepared weekly by diluting single-element stock standard solutions. Calibration standards, reference seawater aliquots, and samples were doped with 115In (0.1 µg L−1) to monitor and correct instrumental drift. 115In correction was used when the instrumental drift was >5%. A Careful rinse (with 2% HNO3) followed by an instrumental background check was performed before every sample measurement to monitor sample to sample memory effects and correct for them, if necessary. Because of the low level of oxides formation, it was not necessary to apply mathematical correction accounting for oxide formation (e.g., UO 0.999, Fig. 3).Fig. 3Linear calibration curves obtained of intensities (cps) measured by The Thermo Scientific™Element XR™ High-Resolution ICP-MS in six-point calibration solutions (certified standard of lanthanoids High-Purity™ Standards).Fig 3

steps.title: Filter and acidify seawater samples
steps.instruction: Collect 1 L of seawater, filter it through a 0.45 µm nylon Whatman® membrane filter using plastic tweezers for each sample, then add 1.5 mL of concentrated HNO₃ to each filtered aliquot to obtain an acidic pH (< 2). Store the acid‑treated samples and blanks for one month to release organic ligands and oxidize metals.

steps.title: Pre‑concentrate lanthanoids with seaFAST‑SP3
steps.instruction: Transfer aliquots of the filtered, acidified seawater into 50 mL polypropylene vials and process them off‑line with the seaFAST‑SP3™ low‑pressure ion‑chromatography system using the conditions listed in Table 1. Run each sample in triplicate.

substeps.instruction: Load the sample vial onto the seaFAST‑SP3™ system.
Use a buffer of NH₄OH/CH₃COOH adjusted to pH 6 ± 0.2.
Set the eluent to 2 N HNO₃; ensure sample pH is < 2 before injection.
Employ a column packed with EDTriA and IDA resin.
Inject an initial sample volume of 10 mL; collect the eluted fraction of 0.2 mL (≈ 20‑fold concentration, up to 50‑fold reported).
Allow 15 min per sample for matrix removal and lanthanoid chelation.

steps.title: Introduce eluted sample to HR‑ICP‑MS
steps.instruction: Using the ESI SC autosampler (4 DX Autosampler with Dual Flowing Rinse), deliver the seaFAST‑SP3™ eluate to the Thermo Scientific™ Element XR™ high‑resolution ICP‑MS via a micro‑Flow PFA nebulizer at 200 µL min⁻¹, passing through a Peltier‑cooled PC3 quartz impact‑bead spray chamber (collision‑reaction cell) before aerosolisation in the argon plasma.

steps.title: Configure HR‑ICP‑MS and perform analysis
steps.instruction: Set the Element XR™ instrument to off‑line, triple‑detector mode with automatic switching, apply the operating parameters in Tables 2‑3, run calibration and blanks, add internal standard, perform rinses, and acquire lanthanoid data.

substeps.instruction: Instrument power settings: RF 1500 W, plasma 1240 W.
Gas flows: cool gas 16 L min⁻¹, auxiliary 0.86 L min⁻¹, sample 1.066 L min⁻¹.
Install nickel cones (ES‑3000‑1812 and 1802) and set the spray chamber to the ESI PC3 Peltier cooler.
Mass‑resolution: low‑detection mode; detector mode: Triple (analog, counting, Faraday).
Set mass window to 150, sample time per peak 0.01 s, 20 masses per peak.

Fine‑tune ion‑optics: focus offset 50 %, Ua/Ub −0.23 %, extraction −2000 V, focus −1049 V, X‑deflection −2.18 V, Y‑deflection −6.09 V, shape 106.5 V, rotation quadrupole 1 = 1.29 V, 2 = −0.87 V, focus quadrupole 1 = −8.69 V, 2 = 0.7 V, MATSUDA‑Plate 150 V, SEM‑depletion 500 V, SEM 2050 V, Guard electrode YES, Faraday deflection −177 V, torch positions X 2.9 mm, Y 0.1 mm, Z −3.9 mm.

Prepare external calibration standards daily from a 10 mg L⁻¹ multi‑element lanthanoid stock (2 % HNO₃) to give six points: 1, 5, 10, 50, 100 and 1000 ng L⁻¹; process these standards through the seaFAST‑SP3™ exactly as samples.
Prepare instrumental blanks of 2 % HNO₃ and NaCl matrix (2 % HNO₃) and measure them before each sample/standard.
Prepare a 100 µg L⁻¹ ¹¹⁵In internal‑standard solution weekly; spike all calibration standards, reference seawater aliquots and samples to 0.1 µg L⁻¹ ¹¹⁵In.
Monitor drift with the ¹¹⁵In signal; apply drift correction when drift exceeds 5 %.
Before each sample run, perform a careful rinse with 2 % HNO₃ and run an instrumental background check to assess memory effects.
Because oxide formation is negligible, no mathematical oxide correction is required.

description: To check the validity of this method, we analyzed estuarine water reference samples (SLEW-3, National Research Council of Canada). Although certified values for lanthanoids are not available for these certified reference materials (CRM), we compared our results with other studies (Table 4; [1,2,10,12]). The recovery based on the SLEW-3, averaged from 78.6% for Pr to 106% for Ce. Because UV oxidation was not performed in the pre-treatment of the acidified samples, to oxidize natural organic ligands and to dissociate lanthanoids of ligands [5], a low recovery for several elements can be explained by the presence of complex organic in seawater. Also, the external accuracy was assessed via repeat analyses of an artificial seawater sample (NaCl matrix, 35 g L−1). Column recovery was evaluated using 100 ng L−1 multi-element lanthanoid standard solutions, and the artificial sample means recoveries ranged from 95 to 100% (Fig. 4). Exceptions were observed for Ce and Lu (recovery 105–110%) and Pr and Dy (recovery 87–90%). The coefficient of variation (CV, %) for every lanthanoid in samples was ≤10% (10 repeated analyses of the artificial seawater sample), except for Gd, Tb and Yb (11–13.75%) (Table 3). The blanks varied between 0.01 and 0.07 ng L−1. Blanks represent <5% of the SLEW- values and <1% in the synthetic seawater.
